liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Black Peter** (3 reviews): Reviewer calls this Black Peter among the best they have heard, live or on tape; First-time concertgoer felt euphoric and could not stop smiling during this song [12][19][23]
- **Friend Of The Devil** (1 review): Jerry's singing and playing on this song come across as especially sweet [12]

## Setlist highlights

- **Tapers Comments**: earliest performance in the archive; mythic rare: 2 archived performances [24]

## The recordings

- **gd1991-04-27.fob.schoepsCMC32.young.GEMS.93470.flac16** (recommended): source not stated; 20 songs; 183 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd91-04-27.sbd.miller.26332.sbeok.flacf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 170 min; rated 3.5/5 by 8 [2]. Said about its sound: This matrix version is far better in sound and continuity than the other soundboard on the archive, crisper and more dynamic; Opening song's first seconds sound like a typical weak outdoor recording, then it turns seamlessly into direct-soundboard quality for the rest [20][22]
- **gd91-04-27.sbd.vernon-fink.12018.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 19 songs; 165 min; rated 4.29/5 by 17 [5]. Said about its sound: Mostly soundboard with a few audience patches that are not bothersome; Somewhat funky recording: mostly soundboard with well-done audience patches spliced in; The show's start sounded a bit off until the sound system kicked in properly [12][13][18]
- **gd1991-04-27.156404.sbd.cm.miller.t.flac1644**: soundboard; 19 songs; 170 min [6]
- **gd1991-04-27.sbd.vernon.6111.shnf**: soundboard; 19 songs; 151 min; rated 1.5/5 by 2 [10]. Said about its sound: Notes flag Garcia's vocals switching channels early, a gap in a first vocal, and a cut from Uncle John's Band into Space [10]

## Around the show

- Sound trouble in the desert plagued Dan Healey early in set one, but the show gained momentum through the day [13]
- Attendee recalls a relaxed, hassle-free atmosphere, apart from a bad traffic jam for anyone taking a wrong turn arriving [14]
- Held in April, so the heat was bearable; open desert, hills and colorful crowd suited the Dead [15]
- Sun set over the mountains with a truly red sky; band and crowd seemed to feed each other's energy [19]
- A couple married at the show and shared their wedding cake with fans; there was a gorgeous sunset [21]
- A sound problem was fixed after Friend Of The Devil, and the show then got rolling [23]
- After several years away from Las Vegas, this was the first of many Dead shows there in following years [13]
- The band had not played Las Vegas for over ten years; this was the first of two shows that weekend [21]
- Reviewer finds the show pretty standard for 1991, with nothing setting it apart [22]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1991-04-27.fob.schoepsCMC32.young.GEMS.93470.flac16**: taped by James Young; transferred by Todd Evans, Jamie Waddell; source: (FOB) Schoeps CMC 32 Omni (on stands 6' 2" high and spaced 8 feet) > Panasonic sv250 [1]
- **gd91-04-27.sbd.miller.26332.sbeok.flacf**: source: 3 source combo: 1: SBD> Dat> Cassette Master> Dat (48k); 2: SBD> Dat> Sonic Solutions> CD; 3: (FOB) Schoeps CMC3/MK2> Dat (48k); Transfer: Dat or CD> SEK'D… [2]. Also: Three-source combo: soundboard to DAT and cassette master, soundboard to CD, and a front-of-board Schoeps DAT; transferred and edited by Charlie Miller [2]
- **gd91-04-27.sbd.vernon-fink.12018.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD material from [5]
- **gd1991-04-27.156404.sbd.cm.miller.t.flac1644**: taped by Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  April 2, 2022; source: SBD > Cassette Master (TDK SA-X100) [6]. Also: Patch source was recorded by James Young; this release is converted from a 24-bit/96k version to 16-bit/44.1k FLAC [6]
- **gd1991-04-27.sbd.vernon.6111.shnf**: transferred by Matt Vernon; source: SBD> Phil Lesh's cassette master>DAT>CDR [10]
